terms.gloss: let me catch my breath, please

phrases.latin: «Sinite respīrem, quaesō,» inquit. «Vōs mūrōs ascendite; ego hīc vōs exspectābō.»
phrases.english: “Let me catch my breath, please,” he said. “You go up on the walls; I’ll wait for you here.”
phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 95, 287.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
